_doc: News and rumour. news.item.* are gossip lines about events read from the world (speaker = whoever tells it); vars: {who} {whofull} {baby} {babe} {mother} {mothfirst} {father} {age} {cause} {widow} {groom} {bride} {groomfull} {bridefull} {title} {from} {ill} {good} {there}. Tags: great (rank 5+), far, died, infant, young, old, childbed, plague, widowed, woman, man. news.deed.* are rumours of what someone did; vars {who} {whofull} {other}.

ask: What's the talk of {place} these days?

lead.t: I'll tell you what I've heard.
Only what the wind brings, but:

none.t: Quiet times, thank God. Not a word to report.
A dull week. If I hear anything, you'll be the first.
I've heard nothing new since the last holy day.
Not a thing, {addr}. A thin season for gossip.

birth: {Mother} was brought to bed of {baby}, {who}, and both are doing well.
A child was born to {mother}: {baby}, they've named {who}.
There's a new babe at {mothfirst}'s hearth — {baby}, called {who}.
God has sent {mother} {baby}; {who} is the name.

birth.t: Great news from the hall: {baby} is born to {mother}, and the house rejoices.
Poor {mothfirst} bore {baby}, {who}, but the little one did not live.
{Who} came into the world this week, a squalling {babe}, they say. Strong lungs.

birth: A babe at {mothfirst}'s door this week — {baby}, and thriving.
{Who}, {baby}, born to {mother}. Easy labour, they say.
death: {Whofull} has passed on, aged {age}. God rest the soul.
{Whofull} died {cause}, aged {age}. The bell has tolled.
We buried {whofull} this week. {Age} years. God keep them.

death.t: Old {who} is gone to God at last, aged {age}. A long life.
{Who} died in childbed. God comfort the household.
The plague took {whofull}. Folk are afraid.
A babe, {who}, was lost this week. God keep the little one.
{Whofull} is dead, so young. Barely {age}. What a pity.
{Whofull} is dead, and {widow} is left alone. Be kind to them.
A lord has died: {whofull}. The land will not be quiet for long.

death: {Whofull} is no more. Aged {age}, God rest them.
The bell tolled for {who} this week.

death.t: The old ones are going, one by one. {Who} was {age}.

wedding: {Groomfull} and {bridefull} were wed, and the whole street feasted.
{Groom} has taken {bride} to wife. They say it was a good match.
There's been a wedding: {bridefull} and {groomfull}. The ale ran freely.

wedding.t: A great match: {groomfull} and {bridefull}, with the lords of both houses present.

wedding: {Bride} is married, God bless her, to {groom}. Mark my words, there'll be a baby by Michaelmas.
{Bridefull} and {groomfull} are wed. The feast lasted till dawn.
expecting: {Who} is with child, they say, and due before long.
There'll be a new voice in {who}'s house soon; she's expecting.
{Who} is great with child. The midwife has been twice.
{Who} is expecting; the midwife is already counting days.
Another cradle to be rocked in {who}'s house, God willing.
sick: {Who} lies sick of {ill}. Pray for them.
Poor {who} has {ill}, and no one holds out much hope.
{Who} has taken to bed with {ill}. Keep clear, if you're wise.
{Who} is poorly with {ill}. They'd be glad of a prayer.
reeve: {Who} is chosen reeve for the year. May he be fair.
We have a new reeve: {who}. Let's see how long the goodwill lasts.
{Who} carries the reeve's staff now. They say he'll not be bought.
The reeve's staff passes to {who}. We shall see.
{Who}, as reeve, will have his hands full this year.
inherit: {Who} now holds {title}, after {from}. We shall see what manner of lord that makes.
{Who} has inherited {title}. The old order changes.
{Title} has a new master: {who}. May God guide his hand.
{Who} now sits where {from} sat, as holder of {title}.
price_dear: {Good} is dear at market this week. Folk grumble.
The price of {good} climbs. Buy early.
Dear, the {good}. Dearer than last season.
Not a penny's worth of {good} but costs two now.
price_cheap: {Good} is cheap at market. A bargain for the quick.
There's plenty of {good} about, and the price shows it.
The price of {good} has fallen. Good for buyers, bad for sellers.
Go and buy {good}; it's a giveaway at present.

alms: They say {whofull} gave alms at the church door; a good soul.
{Whofull} has been generous to the poor. Folk speak well of it.
Someone left coin for the poor, and the name whispered is {who}.
{Whofull} gave to the poor, they say, with a full hand.
insult: They say {whofull} spoke ill to {other} before witnesses. A hot head.
{Whofull} and {other} had words, and not kind ones.
Did you hear? {Who} insulted {other} to their face.
Hard words were spoken by {who} to {other}. Stay clear of both.
threat: {Whofull} threatened {other}, folk say. Best keep clear.
There was ugly talk between {who} and {other}. Threats were made.
{Who} has a hard way with {other}, they say. Mind your tongue near them.
{Whofull} was heard threatening {other}. That's a bad business.
wed: {Whofull} and {other} are wed, the talk of the week.
{Who} has married {other}. Half the parish is still singing.
A wedding! {Whofull} and {other}. Long life to them.
{Who} and {other}, man and wife. The village is merry.
other: There's gossip about {who}, but I'll not repeat it.
They say {whofull} is a name to watch.
They talk of {who} in the alehouse, and not softly.
